note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • 3-day history of worsening bifrontal/right-periocular headache; no clear precipitating trigger identified.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Began at work 3 days ago; gradually intensified and now constant with intermittent surges of greater intensity (rated 8/10 at worst).
  • Photophobia noted since onset (“hurts to look at bright lights”); “shooting lights” reported at start.
  • Ibuprofen taken for 2 days provided no relief.
- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: Denied.
  • Voice change/hoarseness: Denied.
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling: Denied.
  • Nasal/ocular: Photophobia; no nasal obstruction/discharge reported.
  • Stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea: Denied.
  • Facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling: Denied.
  • Ear symptoms/hearing change: Not mentioned.
  • Neck pain/stiffness: Denied.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • Prior headaches responsive to ibuprofen; no previous similar unrelieved episode.
  • No prior ED visits, hospitalizations, or injection therapies for headache.
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Drug/food/environmental allergies: None known.
  • Current medications: None routinely. Ibuprofen self-initiated (3 tablets/day; dose/strength/route/frequency otherwise not documented).
- Social context:
  • Lives with three housemates; employed in IT (computer work); recent moderate work stress; socially smokes and drinks.

Objective:
- Observable swelling/distribution: Not noted.
- Airway/breathing: No stridor or respiratory distress reported.
- Mental status: Alert; reports difficulty focusing due to pain.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded.
- Accompaniment: Patient attended alone (teleconsultation).

Assessment:
- Probable migraine-type headache given unilateral predominance, photophobia, family history of migraines, lack of response to sub-therapeutic NSAID dosing.
- No red-flag ENT or neurological features (no neck stiffness, focal deficit, visual loss, airway compromise).

Plan:
- Medication:
  • Counselled on correct ibuprofen dosing (up to 400 mg ×2 tablets three times daily with food; dose/route/frequency explained).
  • Offer prescription for stronger NSAID (naproxen) ± paracetamol/codeine combination; patient agreeable.
- Symptom/trigger monitoring:
  • Keep daily headache diary (onset, duration, potential triggers, medication use, response).
- Red-flag advice:
  • Seek immediate medical attention (call clinic or emergency services) for visual disturbance, limb weakness, speech difficulty, escalating severity, new neck stiffness, vomiting, or any airway/breathing concerns.
- Follow-up:
  • Review in 1–2 weeks; earlier if headaches persist/worsen.
  • Discuss prophylactic therapy at follow-up if headaches become recurrent.
- Lifestyle/other:
  • Suggested eye exam due to longstanding glasses use and screen work.
  • Hydration, stress management, and screen-brightness adjustment reinforced.

Quality checks:
• Missing but expected elements: 
  – Formal neurological/ENT physical examination (fundoscopy, cranial nerves, otoscopy, nasal inspection, neck palpation).
  – Detailed ibuprofen dose (mg) and tablet strength.
  – Documentation of visual acuity or eye exam findings.
  – Availability/use of migraine-specific agents (e.g., triptans) not discussed.
• Internal conflicts: None noted.
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minimal background noise; no major inaudible segments.
